The code to reproduce these analyses is available for free through Github.2 • Using these interactions, we propose and fit a simple but effective energy model of the energy consumption of fully connected neural networks. P • Merging energy measurements with the BUTTER dataset, (C. Tripp, Perr-Sauer, Hayne, et al. 2022), we char- acterize the impact of hyperparameter choice on energy efficiency across all training tasks and architectures, and identify some counter-intuitive results. • We use these results to motivate and propose research directions in energy-efficient architectures, algorithms, and hardware to meet the rising challenge of “Red AI”. The rest of this paper is structured as follows: Section 2 discusses related work. Section 3 describes the BUTTER-E dataset and method used to collect and compile the data. Section 4 describes how the data was prepared for the anal- ysis in this paper, presenting practical challenges and the techniques we used to standardize and compare real-world computational energy measurements in a large HPC system. Section 5 discusses observed aggregate relationships between hyperparameter (and dataset) choice and energy consumption. Section 6 provides a detailed analysis of the interaction between cache size and energy consumption by linking network topology defined factors to critical work- ing sets and mapping those working sets onto the memory hierarchy.
